\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{پیامد} (payâmad)}{پیامد (payâmad)}]{\fa{پیامد} (payâmad) — a consequence, an outcome}

\label{lesson:FA-C370-payamad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to bring about, then the Persian for owing to.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{پیامد}}
\textbf{\fa{پیامد}} (\emph{payâmad}) — \textquotedblleft{}a consequence, an outcome\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{این} \fa{تصمیم} \fa{پیامدهای} \fa{مهمی} \fa{داشت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{in tasmim payâmadhâ-ye mohemmi dâsht.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This decision had important consequences.
\end{quote}

Native and formal: \emph{pay} \textquotedblleft{}trace, footstep\textquotedblright{} + \emph{âmad} \textquotedblleft{}came\textquotedblright{}. Plural \emph{payâmadhâ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{پیامد}} is a native Persian compound built from \emph{pay} \textquotedblleft{}footstep, trace\textquotedblright{} and \emph{âmad}, the past stem of \emph{âmadan} \textquotedblleft{}to come\textquotedblright{}, which EtymDB traces to PIE \emph{g\textsuperscript{w}em-} \textquotedblleft{}to step\textquotedblright{}: what comes in the footsteps of an act.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{payâmad}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{payâmad}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to bring about, then the Persian for owing to, then say \emph{payâmad} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{عواقب} ('avâqeb)}{عواقب ('avâqeb)}]{\fa{عواقب} ('avâqeb) — repercussions, bad consequences}

\label{lesson:FA-C370-avaqeb}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for owing to, then the Persian for a consequence.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{عواقب}}
\textbf{\fa{عواقب}} (\emph{'avâqeb}) — \textquotedblleft{}repercussions, bad consequences\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{به} \fa{عواقب} \fa{کارش} \fa{فکر} \fa{نکرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u be 'avâqeb-e kârash fekr nakard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He did not think about the consequences of his action.
\end{quote}

An Arabic broken plural of \emph{'âqebat} \textquotedblleft{}end, outcome\textquotedblright{}. In nearly every case the consequences are bad ones.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{عواقب}} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{'awāqib}, a broken plural of \emph{'āqiba} \textquotedblleft{}end, outcome\textquotedblright{}: what follows at the end.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{'avâqeb}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{'avâqeb}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{'avâqeb}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for owing to, then the Persian for a consequence, then say \emph{'avâqeb} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{عواقب} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Repercussions, bad consequences\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{در} \fa{نتیجه} (dar natije)}{در نتیجه (dar natije)}]{\fa{در} \fa{نتیجه} (dar natije) — as a result, consequently}

\label{lesson:FA-C370-dar-natije}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a consequence, then the Persian for repercussions.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{در} \fa{نتیجه}}
\textbf{\fa{در} \fa{نتیجه}} (\emph{dar natije}) — \textquotedblleft{}as a result, consequently\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{زیاد} \fa{کار} \fa{کرد} \fa{و} \fa{در} \fa{نتیجه} \fa{بیمار} \fa{شد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u ziyâd kâr kard va dar natije bimâr shod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He worked too much, and as a result he fell ill.
\end{quote}

\emph{Dar} \textquotedblleft{}in\textquotedblright{} + \emph{natije} \textquotedblleft{}result\textquotedblright{}. A whole clause follows; \emph{dar natije-ye} + noun means \textquotedblleft{}as a result of\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{در} \fa{نتیجه}} joins the inherited Persian preposition \emph{dar} \textquotedblleft{}in\textquotedblright{} to \emph{natije}, from Arabic \emph{natīja} \textquotedblleft{}result\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB): in the result.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dar natije}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dar natije}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{dar natije}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a consequence, then the Persian for repercussions, then say \emph{dar natije} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{در} \fa{نتیجه} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}As a result, consequently\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{منجر} \fa{شدن} (monjar shodan)}{منجر شدن (monjar shodan)}]{\fa{منجر} \fa{شدن} (monjar shodan) — to lead to, to result in}

\label{lesson:FA-C370-monjar-shodan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for repercussions, then the Persian for as a result.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{منجر} \fa{شدن}}
\textbf{\fa{منجر} \fa{شدن}} (\emph{monjar shodan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to lead to, to result in\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{این} \fa{اشتباه} \fa{به} \fa{یک} \fa{دعوای} \fa{بزرگ} \fa{منجر} \fa{شد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{in eshtebâh be yek da'vâ-ye bozorg monjar shod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This mistake led to a big quarrel.
\end{quote}

Takes \emph{be}: \emph{be chizi monjar shodan}. Formal. Stem \emph{shav-}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{منجر}} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{munjarr} \textquotedblleft{}drawn along\textquotedblright{}; with the Persian verb \emph{shodan} \textquotedblleft{}to become\textquotedblright{}, one thing is drawn along into another.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{monjar shodan}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for repercussions, then the Persian for as a result, then say \emph{monjar shodan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{نتیجه} \fa{گرفتن} (natije gereftan)}{نتیجه گرفتن (natije gereftan)}]{\fa{نتیجه} \fa{گرفتن} (natije gereftan) — to conclude, to infer}

\label{lesson:FA-C370-natije-gereftan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for as a result, then the Persian for to lead to.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{نتیجه} \fa{گرفتن}}
\textbf{\fa{نتیجه} \fa{گرفتن}} (\emph{natije gereftan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to conclude, to infer\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{از} \fa{حرفهای} \fa{او} \fa{نتیجه} \fa{گرفتم} \fa{که} \fa{خسته} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{az harfhâ-ye u natije gereftam ke khaste ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
From what he said I concluded that he was tired.
\end{quote}

\emph{Natije} \textquotedblleft{}result\textquotedblright{} + \emph{gereftan} \textquotedblleft{}to take\textquotedblright{} (present stem \emph{gir-}). Also to get results.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{نتیجه} \fa{گرفتن}} is literally \textquotedblleft{}to take a result\textquotedblright{}: \emph{natije} comes from Arabic \emph{natīja} \textquotedblleft{}result\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), and \emph{gereftan} \textquotedblleft{}to take\textquotedblright{} is the inherited Persian verb.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
